meta.verified: Alerts read from the TradingView alert log (4H chart alerts only). Prices are 1-minute bars. Entry is the first 1-minute price after the alert. For metals I count 1 pip as $1.00 for gold and $0.10 for silver, so they sit on a similar scale to forex pips. That scale is my choice, not a market standard. The 11 alerts from 16-17 Nov keep their original entry prices. The 3 newer alerts use the open of the first 1-minute bar after the alert, which can differ from the original method by up to about 2 pips. A stop counts as reached if any 1-minute high or low touched it. The table itself keeps each alert running until the opposite alert, so it does not stop trades out. The EURUSD row (19 Nov 02:00) uses the highest high and lowest low of the 02:00, 06:00 and 10:00 4H candles, read by hand from the chart, and the price at 10:55 HK, so it is less exact than the others. The GBPUSD row (18 Nov 10:00) also uses hand-read highs and lows from the seven 4H candles since the alert, and the price at 11:34 HK. | UPDATE 19 Nov 20:08 HK: Now / at close refreshed from the chart price on the 20:06-20:08 screenshots. For older rows, best and worst were only widened where the new price went past them, so they are lower bounds. The five new CAUTION rows use the exact entry, stop and target from the Discord alerts, and best/worst from the live 4H candle. Forex 4H bars close at 02, 06, 10, 14, 18, 22 HK; gold and silver close one hour later (03, 07, 11, 15, 19, 23). | UPDATE 19 Nov 22:08 HK: Now / at close refreshed again from the 22:06-22:08 screenshots; best and worst are still lower bounds. No new 4H alert showed on any forex dashboard at the 22:00 close. | UPDATE 20 Nov 09:05 HK: Now / at close refreshed from the 09:04-09:05 screenshots. Best and worst were widened with the high and low of the current 06:00 4H candle only, so they are still lower bounds (the 22:00, 02:00 and 06:00 candles are not all read). A row counts as stopped if that widened worst move reached the alert stop.

alerts.context: CAUTION: counter-trend (close below the slow MA 107.589)

findings.title: 09:05 HK refresh: the CAUTION label was right
findings.body: 2 of 22 rows are up now. All six v2.34 CAUTION alerts are underwater: AUDJPY 14:00 buy -67.3, AUDJPY 18:00 buy -116.7, GBPUSD 18:00 buy -52.5, USDCAD 18:00 sell -28.0, AUDUSD 18:00 buy -50.3, XAUUSD 19:00 buy -150.4. 5 of the six have reached their stop on the lower-bound measure (AUDJPY 14:00, AUDJPY 18:00, GBPUSD 18:00, AUDUSD 18:00, XAUUSD 19:00). Only the USDCAD sell is still open. This is the first evidence that CAUTION (counter-trend) was a useful warning, but it is six alerts in one falling market, so it is not a rule yet. One new 4H alert shows on the dashboards: USDJPY T1 SELL CAUTION at 02:00 HK (entry not added; needs the Discord text). No other 4H alert fired at the 22:00, 02:00 or 06:00 closes.

findings.title: 22:08 HK refresh
findings.body: 12 of 22 rows are up now. No new 4H alert fired at the 22:00 forex close. The six CAUTION alerts after 2 to 8 hours: AUDJPY 14:00 buy +63.4, AUDJPY 18:00 buy +14.0, GBPUSD 18:00 buy +13.9, USDCAD 18:00 sell +15.0, AUDUSD 18:00 buy +7.8, XAUUSD 19:00 buy -23.3. CVD correction: the earlier note said CVD agreed on all six, but that used the delta of one bar. Using the 5-bar CVD trend at the time of each alert (v2.36 dashboard), 2 agree (AUDJPY 18:00, AUDUSD), 2 are flat (GBPUSD, USDCAD) and 1 is against (XAUUSD). AUDJPY 14:00 is not shown on the dashboard any more. Too few alerts to judge the label.

findings.title: 20:08 HK refresh
findings.body: 11 of 22 rows are up now. Six v2.34 alerts have fired and all six are CAUTION (counter-trend), and the one-bar CVD delta pointed the same way on all six (the 5-bar CVD trend is mixed, see the 22:08 note). After 2 to 6 hours: AUDJPY 14:00 buy +56.6, AUDJPY 18:00 buy +7.2, GBPUSD buy +5.8, AUDUSD buy +1.7, USDCAD sell +0.6, XAUUSD buy -14.4. Too early to judge the label. The CAUTION buy on AUDJPY has not been right so far.

findings.title: First CAUTION alert (v2.34), 19 Nov 14:00
findings.body: AUDJPY 4H T1 buy, entry 106.710, marked CAUTION because the close was 88 pips below the slow MA. Best and worst figures come from the 14:00 4H candle read by hand at 14:16, so they are early. This row will show whether the CAUTION label was right.

findings.title: What is in the table
findings.body: 16 alerts on the 4H chart from Mon 16 Nov to Thu 19 Nov 02:00 HK: 14 Tier 1, 1 Tier 2 and 1 Tier 3. 11 are Tier 1 buys, 3 are Tier 1 USDCAD sells, plus the Tier 2 CADJPY sell and the Tier 3 GBPUSD sell. All 16 are still running, because no opposite alert of the same tier has fired.

findings.title: Two rows are less exact
findings.body: The EURUSD and GBPUSD rows use highs and lows read by hand from 4H candles, because the price feed hit its daily limit. Their best and worst figures can be off by a pip or two. The other 14 rows use 1-minute prices.

findings.title: Where they stand now
findings.body: Only 2 of 16 are above entry: the GBPUSD Tier 3 sell, +77.7 pips (best +85.9), and the CADJPY Tier 2 sell, +47.9 pips (best +60.0). 13 of 16 touched their stop price at some point, and none reached its target. The 11 Tier 1 buys average +14.5 pips at their best and 105.7 pips worst against, and are now -79.5 on average. Most were fired into a falling market on 16-17 Nov.

findings.title: The only winners are Tier 2 and Tier 3 sells
findings.body: Both winning alerts are sells in the direction of the 4H down trend, and both are trend-following tiers, not the Tier 1 exhaustion signal. That is two alerts, so it is a lead to test, not a rule.

findings.title: USDCAD sells against the up trend
findings.body: The three Tier 1 USDCAD sells (17 Nov 14:00 and 18:00, 18 Nov 22:00) were fired against a 4H up trend. They reached their stops at 00:40, 00:37 and 10:57 HK on 19 Nov, after best-in-favour moves of only 23.6, 20.7 and 2.6 pips.

findings.title: Too few alerts to draw a rule
findings.body: About three and a half trading days. GBPJPY, AUDJPY and USDJPY each fired more than once in the same direction, so the buys are closer to 8 ideas than 11. Nearly all were buys in one falling market, so this says little about Tier 1 in other conditions. Every number moves until opposite alerts arrive.
